channel.title: WSJ | World
channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: The Political Taboo Tearing France Apart
item.description: France has long refused to talk about race. The finger pointing over the riots may be its wake-up call for a new approach.

item.title: Denmark Accuses Russia of Trying to Kill Ukrainian Rapper
item.description: The alleged plot is the latest example of a Western country accusing Moscow of orchestrating a crime on European soil.

item.title: Indian Man Sentenced to Almost 20 Years in Murder-for-Hire Plot on U.S. Soil
item.description: Prosecutors said Nikhil Gupta was part of a plot that targeted a number of Sikhs living outside India over their political beliefs.

item.title: El Salvador Takes Its Gang-Fighting Strategy to Haiti
item.description: The Central American country has deployed more than 2,500 troops to the anarchic Caribbean nation.

item.title: How the Myanmar Genocide Ruling Raises the Stakes for Israel
item.description: The most-watched aspect of the case was how the International Court of Justice would determine Myanmar’s intent to commit genocide against the Rohingya.

item.title: New Satellite Photos Show Expansion of North Korean Uranium-Enrichment Plant
item.description: Images show a new extension attached to the main enrichment hall at the Yongbyon nuclear complex, according to an analysis by The Wall Street Journal.

item.title: American State Capitalism Helped Produce the Nvidia Scandal
item.description: Under Trump, government and corporate interests have become more tightly intertwined. The Nvidia backlash may halt that.

item.title: Eurozone Wage Growth Accelerates, But Remains Modest
item.description: Negotiated wage growth accelerated to 2.57% in the third quarter from 2.45% in the previous quarter, according to the ECB.

item.title: EU Open to ‘Closest Possible Relationship’ With U.K., Chief Says
item.description: European Council President Antonio Costa said Europe would respect whatever decision the U.K. takes about its future ties with the bloc.

item.title: The U.S. Is Auctioning Off a Slice of the Pacific Ocean Floor in Push for Minerals
item.description: The Trump administration sold 31.5 million acres of seabed near American Samoa to unlock new sources of metals and minerals.

item.title: After Brexit, Britain’s Government Floats ‘Breturn’
item.description: The U.K.’s European psychodrama is about to return as Prime Minister Andy Burnham kick-starts a debate on rejoining the EU.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts of November 2026: Up to 5.00%
item.description: Beat average interest rates with one of these top high-yield savings accounts.

item.title: Russia Steps Up Attacks on Kyiv’s Bridges
item.description: The latest missile barrage comes after Ukraine damaged a key bridge linking Crimea to Russia.

item.title: U.S. Has Floated NATO Membership for Ukraine in Recent Meetings
item.description: President Trump’s envoys discussed Ukraine surrendering territory in the Donbas in exchange for NATO membership, a reversal of longstanding U.S. policy.

item.title: U.K. Government Borrowed More in October, But Is on Track for Smaller Deficit
item.description: At 3.5% of gross domestic product, the budget deficit for the fiscal year to October was lower than the 3.8% recorded a year earlier.

item.title: Spain Remains Europe’s Star Economy. Why Don’t People Feel Richer?
item.description: Spain’s economy continues to boast growth rates that are the envy of Europe. But as discontent continues to mount over living standards ahead of next week’s elections, it is clear that not everyone is celebrating.

item.title: Trump Escapes Turmoil at Home by Seeking Out a Friendlier Audience Abroad
item.description: The president is expected to increasingly turn to foreign policy to cement his legacy as he faces gridlock in Washington.

item.title: Houthi Attack Damages Saudi Capital’s Tallest Tower
item.description: The strike damaged several floors in the 80-story building which houses the kingdom’s sovereign-wealth fund.

item.title: Israeli Spy Chief Pressed for Renewed Iran Strikes During U.S. Visit
item.description: As Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu advocates for more bombing, Gulf countries are pushing for a deal.

item.title: Trump-Xi Summit Shows Putin’s Powerful Friendships Have Their Limits
item.description: The trilateral meeting in China with President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping marked a coup for the Russian leader—but he has little concrete to show for it.
